subject.title: fix(tools): surface empty availability group diagnostics via onHiddenDiagnostic callback

question: Should this PR be the canonical fix for https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/92361 and treat plugin-authored `availability`-like records as warn-only OpenClaw availability metadata?
rationale: The implementation is coherent and tested, but deciding whether undeclared plugin-tool metadata should be interpreted by core—and selecting it over the narrower overlapping implementation—requires owner intent rather than an automated code repair.

options.title: Accept the integrated path
options.body: Keep the planner callback plus cached and uncached registration wiring, accepting warn-only interpretation of availability-like plugin metadata.

options.title: Choose the narrower sibling
options.body: Prefer https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94099 for the generic callback and evaluator guards, then handle production plugin wiring through a separate owner-approved change.

options.title: Reject implicit metadata ownership
options.body: Keep undeclared plugin-tool availability metadata ignored and design a different explicitly contracted plugin authoring-diagnostic boundary.

recommendation.title: Accept the integrated path
recommendation.body: Keep the planner callback plus cached and uncached registration wiring, accepting warn-only interpretation of availability-like plugin metadata.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects this owner most strongly to the plugin metadata, descriptor-cache, and manifest control-plane boundaries where the compatibility choice lands.
